theory.title: Ways to add CSS to a page

blocks.content: A language that describes **how HTML elements are displayed**: colours, fonts, sizes, spacing and layout. Separating style from content makes websites easier to maintain.

items.content:
Written in the `style` attribute of one element. `

items.title: Internal (embedded) CSS
items.content:
Written in a `<style>` element in the `<head>` of **one page**.
`<style> p { color: red; } </style>`

items.title: External CSS
items.content:
Written in a separate **.css file** linked to **many pages**.
`<link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">`

blocks.title: Why "cascading"?
blocks.content: When several rules apply to the same element, the browser decides which wins: **inline** beats **internal/external**, a more **specific** selector beats a general one, and a **later** rule beats an earlier one with the same specificity.

For "compare CSS implementation types", the key point is **external CSS = one file controls the whole site** (consistent, easy to update, cached), while **inline CSS** must be repeated in every element.
